text: So here's how it works at the moment. A customer rings or fills in the form on the website, one of the front desk staff writes it on a pad, then at the end of the day someone types the pad into the spreadsheet. If it's a repeat customer we look them up by hand. Reminders go out by text the day before, also by hand. We're nine people across two shops and it's taking too long.
label: in_scope

text: I run a small accountancy practice, six of us, and the problem is the paper. Clients drop off forms, receipts and signed sheets, and a junior re-types them into our ledger software. That's maybe two hours a day of typing and it's where the mistakes come from. I'd like to know whether the document data entry module would cope with our forms and what it would cost per month.
label: in_scope

text: We're a heating and plumbing firm, 28 people counting the office. Jobs come into a shared inbox, someone prints a job sheet, a van goes out, then the sheet gets typed into the field service tool at night. The tool can export but it can't import anything, which I gather is a problem. What are my options there and does it change the price?
label: in_scope

text: Before I go any further I want to understand your pricing. Is it a flat monthly fee per module, does volume change it, and is the setup fee charged once or every year? We looked at another system last year and the surprise costs killed it. I'd rather know the low, base and high numbers up front, even if they're rough.
label: in_scope

text: Our biggest headache is the phones. Between eight and ten in the morning we miss maybe a third of the calls because the two receptionists are checking people in. Those callers go elsewhere. I'm told the phone intake module can take those calls and book them. What does it actually do when a caller wants a specific groomer, or wants to change an existing booking?
label: in_scope

text: To answer your question about mistakes: mostly missed and duplicated. A request comes in by email and by phone from the same customer and we book it twice, or a message sits in the inbox over the weekend and nobody sees it until Tuesday. Wrong details are rarer, maybe once a week, usually a phone number typed wrong. Delayed is the big one in winter.
label: in_scope

text: We have a web form, a shared inbox, and a landline that rings in the shop. About 60 requests a day in season, maybe 20 in January. Each one takes five minutes to deal with and then two or three to type up. There are 14 of us, one site, and I approve anything that involves a refund or a discount over ten percent.
label: in_scope

text: I don't want anything sending messages to my customers without me seeing the wording first. We've had a bad experience. If the status update module can use templates I approve and only those, then fine, but I want to understand the opt-out part too, because some of our older clients don't want texts at all. How does that side work?
label: in_scope

text: Let me walk you through a typical job. The customer emails, the office replies asking for photos, the customer sends them, we price it, I approve it if it's over a thousand, we book a van, the engineer does the job and fills in a paper sheet, the office types the sheet into the system and raises the invoice. Nine steps, three of which are typing.
label: in_scope

text: What I'm hoping to automate is the triage. Not the replies, not the pricing, just reading the inbox and sorting what's urgent from what isn't, and creating a ticket for each one so nothing gets lost. We tried colour-coded flags in the mailbox and it lasted a fortnight. Would the email triage module and the ticket creation module cover that together, or is one enough?
label: in_scope

text: Something I should say about personal data. We keep customers' names, addresses, phone numbers and in some cases card details on file for regulars. We also have notes on pets that are nervous or need medication. If your system reads our spreadsheet, where does that data go, who can see it, and can I delete it later? I need to be able to answer that to my customers.
label: in_scope

text: I've answered most of your questions now. Can you tell me where the report stands and what's still missing before you can give an estimate? I'd like to submit before Friday because my business partner is away next week and we want to decide on a start date together. If something's blocking the quote, tell me what and I'll find the number.
label: in_scope

text: We're not a trade, we're a small clinic, three practitioners and two on reception. Requests are appointment bookings, cancellations and prescription queries, roughly 80 a day by phone and email. Nothing goes through a spreadsheet, we have a practice management system that can export CSV but I don't think it has an API. Does that matter for what you'd propose?
label: in_scope

text: The staffing side is what I want to look at. We have twelve engineers with different skills, gas, electrical, general plumbing, and the dispatcher assigns jobs from memory. When she's off, the wrong person gets sent and we lose half a day. I read the staff assignment description. Can it hold skills and availability per person, and can the office override what it suggests?
label: in_scope

text: Honestly the main goal is time. Not cost, we can afford to pay for this, and errors are annoying but survivable. What I can't get back is the three hours a day my manager spends on the phone and the inbox instead of on the floor with the team. If a couple of modules give me most of that back, I'm interested. Which ones would you start with?
label: in_scope

text: Urgent requests, yes, we have them. No heat in winter, a smell of gas, a burst pipe. At the moment the emergency line goes to whoever is on call, which rotates weekly, and the office finds out the next morning. I want those routed properly and logged, but I don't want a machine deciding what's an emergency. Who decides what counts as urgent in your setup?
label: in_scope

text: Quick question on integrations before we go on. Our booking tool is one of those web widgets that can export a CSV of the day's bookings. No import, no API as far as I know. Your article on export-only tools says results must be re-keyed or pushed through a file drop. What does a file drop mean in practice, and does it add to the setup fee?
label: in_scope

text: I'd like to give you the volume properly because I think I confused things earlier. On a normal weekday we take about 19 jobs. Our worst week last winter was 40 a day, and across a month it comes to roughly 400. Please use the monthly figure divided by working days, not the worst week, when you work out the tier.
label: in_scope

text: Here is what the day looks like for the office team. 8am open the inbox, print anything that came in overnight. 9am the dispatcher allocates vans. All day the phone rings and gets written on a pad. 4pm the engineers come back with paper sheets. 5pm to 6:30pm two people type the sheets into the tool and raise invoices. That last bit is what I'd kill first.
label: in_scope

text: I had a look at your case about the grooming salon that stopped missing bookings. We're very similar, two sites, about the same volume, same spreadsheet problem. What I couldn't tell from the case is how long the setup took and whether they had to change their booking widget. Can you tell me what that case did on the integration side, and what it cost them?
label: in_scope

text: You asked which tools we use. A shared inbox for enquiries, a spreadsheet per site for bookings, a card machine that isn't connected to anything, and a paper diary at the front desk that is the real source of truth when the two disagree. We also have a basic accounting package that exports CSV. Nothing talks to anything else, which is the problem.
label: in_scope

text: I want to be careful about approvals. Any quote above a thousand must come to me before it goes out, refunds always come to me, and nobody but me can change a price. If your system creates tickets and drafts replies, that's fine, but I need those three things to need a person. Does the approvals policy let me set that, or is it fixed?
label: in_scope

text: We've grown faster than the office has. Two years ago it was four of us and one van, now it's 22 people, six vans and a second yard across town. The processes are the same ones we used at four people, which is to say the owner's phone and a notebook. I'm not sure where to start, so ask me whatever you need to.
label: in_scope

text: Let me think about what should be automated and what shouldn't. Intake, yes, anything that captures the request and books a slot. Reminders, yes. Ticket tracking, yes. Replying to complaints, no, a person does that. Pricing, no, I quote every job myself. Assigning engineers, maybe, if the office can override it. Does that split map onto your modules?
label: in_scope

text: Our customers complain that they never know where their order is. text: Right, here are the numbers you asked for in one go. 11 people including me, one shop, around 45 requests a day mostly by phone, four minutes to handle each, then two minutes to type up.
